recommendation: Visit a pharmacist for advice about medication usage, dosage instructions, possible side effects and medication storage.
Ask a pharmacist about possible interactions between medications, vitamins, supplements and traditional medicines.
Pharmacists can advise on managing common health conditions and recommend suitable medications when needed.
Inform the pharmacist about any allergies, existing medical conditions and medications currently being taken.
General Practitioners (GPs) can treat many common health conditions.
People with mild to moderate health problems are encouraged to visit a GP first instead of going directly to the Emergency Department.
A GP can assess the patient's condition and refer them to an acute hospital or Urgent Care Centre if necessary.
Patients with emergency symptoms should seek emergency medical attention rather than delaying care to visit a GP.

gpfirst_programme.description: Encourages people with mild to moderate health problems to visit participating GP clinics before going to the Emergency Department.
benefits: Timely medical treatment at a GP clinic.
Referral to an acute hospital or Urgent Care Centre when necessary.
A $50 subsidy on the prevailing ED attendance fee when referred through the GPFirst Programme, subject to programme terms and conditions.
Priority over non-emergency cases at the Emergency Department.
